problem_restatements: CRT decomposition: Computing (a+b) mod p for 9 coprime primes is equivalent to addition in Z/5Z x Z/7Z x ... x Z/31Z. By CRT, these 9 additions are algebraically independent.
Quotient-remainder partition: Each prime p partitions integers into p cosets. Computing mod p means: determine coset indices, add them, fold if sum >= p.
analogy: CRT orthogonal idempotents: basis elements satisfy idempotence, orthogonality, completeness. Architecture mirrors this with learned orthogonal projectors decomposing shared embedding into independent prime-indexed subspaces.

ops: crt_orthogonal_decomposer: Decomposes d-dim embedding into 9 orthogonal subspaces via projection matrices P_i. Orthogonality enforced via column partition of orthogonal matrix Q.
modular_fold_accumulator: Per-channel sum + piecewise fold. s_i = channel_a_i + channel_b_i, then folded_i = s_i - scale_i * ReLU(W_fold_i @ s_i + bias_fold_i).
coset_cardinality_readout: Per-channel linear projection to p_i logits. Output selects channel matching input prime.
plan.layer_arrangement: embed_shared -> {decompose_i -> accumulate_i -> fold_i -> readout_i} x 9 primes in parallel
plan.reasoning: CRT guarantees mod-p computations for distinct primes are algebraically independent. Orthogonal projections encode this independence. Each channel solves single-prime addition. ~1285 params total.

expected_outcome: >95% accuracy across all primes with ~1000-1500 params. Orthogonal channels eliminate inter-prime interference. Monotonic convergence.
falsification: Fails if: (1) decomposer can't learn CRT basis, (2) fold fails for large primes, (3) channels interfere (oscillating accuracy).
look_back: CRT IS the architecture — canonical theorem for simultaneous modular arithmetic.
Generalizes to any coprime moduli set.
One-shot: decompose, add, fold, done. No iteration needed.
